title: Botany
summary: Read a plant the way a botanist does — from cell to organ to whole community — and use structure to explain what the plant is doing.
objectives: Identify plant cell, root, stem, leaf and flower structures and say what each one does.
Trace water, sugar and nutrients through a plant and explain what drives each movement.
Place a plant in its major division from observable features.
Explain photosynthesis and the plant's role in energy and nutrient cycling.
Diagnose a struggling plant from symptoms, distinguishing deficiency from infection.

units.title: Cells and Tissues
units.summary: Everything a plant can do is set by features its cells have and animal cells do not.
objectives: Name the structures that distinguish a plant cell and state each one's function.
Explain how meristems let a plant keep growing where an animal cannot.

lessons.title: The Plant Cell
lessons.objective: Identify the cell wall, chloroplast, central vacuole and plasmodesmata, and explain what each contributes that an animal cell lacks.

lessons.title: Meristems, Growth, and Differentiation
lessons.objective: Distinguish apical from lateral meristems and explain primary versus secondary growth.

units.title: Roots, Stems, and Leaves
units.summary: Three organs, one job each, and every structural detail follows from that job.
objectives: Relate root, stem and leaf anatomy to absorption, support and photosynthesis.
Read a cross-section and name what you are looking at.

lessons.title: Roots: Absorption and Anchorage
lessons.objective: Identify root hairs, cortex, endodermis and the root cap, and explain how water crosses into the vascular cylinder.

lessons.title: Stems: Support and Transport
lessons.objective: Describe stem anatomy and explain how vascular bundle arrangement differs between monocots and dicots.

lessons.title: Leaves: The Photosynthetic Surface
lessons.objective: Identify epidermis, cuticle, mesophyll layers, veins and stomata, and explain the trade-off a stoma manages.

units.title: Moving Water, Sugar, and Nutrients
units.summary: Two transport tissues, two entirely different mechanisms — this is the distinction tests reach for most.
objectives: Contrast xylem and phloem in structure, contents, direction and driving force.
Explain transpiration and what changes its rate.

lessons.title: Xylem and the Transpiration Stream
lessons.objective: Explain how cohesion, adhesion and tension move water upward without the plant spending energy on it.

lessons.title: Phloem and Sugar Transport
lessons.objective: Explain pressure-flow from source to sink and say why phloem transport requires living cells.

lessons.title: Nutrients and What Their Absence Looks Like
lessons.objective: Distinguish macronutrients from micronutrients and read a deficiency from where and how symptoms appear.

units.title: Photosynthesis and Energy
units.summary: The reaction the whole event orbits, and the plant's place in the cycles it drives.
objectives: State the inputs, outputs and location of each stage of photosynthesis.
Explain the plant's role in the carbon and energy cycles.

lessons.title: Photosynthesis: Light and Carbon
lessons.objective: Separate the light-dependent reactions from the Calvin cycle by location, inputs and outputs.

lessons.title: Respiration and the Cycles Plants Drive
lessons.objective: Contrast photosynthesis with cellular respiration and place plants in the carbon and nitrogen cycles.

units.title: Plant Diversity and Reproduction
units.summary: Place any plant in its group from what you can see, and explain how each group reproduces.
objectives: Distinguish the major plant divisions by vascular tissue, seeds and flowers.
Explain alternation of generations and how it shifts across the divisions.

lessons.title: The Major Plant Divisions
lessons.objective: Separate algae, bryophytes, ferns, gymnosperms and angiosperms by vascular tissue, seeds and flowers, and distinguish monocots from dicots.

lessons.title: Alternation of Generations
lessons.objective: Trace the sporophyte and gametophyte stages and explain which dominates in each major group.

lessons.title: Flowers, Pollination, and Seeds
lessons.objective: Identify flower parts and follow the path from pollination through fertilisation to seed and fruit.

units.title: Plants, People, and Problems
units.summary: Plants in competition, plants under attack, and plants put to work.
objectives: Explain how plants compete and respond to their environment.
Distinguish infection from deficiency and describe how crops are modified.

lessons.title: Growth Responses and Competition
lessons.objective: Explain tropisms and hormone action, and describe how plants compete for light, water and nutrients.

lessons.title: Plant Disease, Crops, and GMOs
lessons.objective: Distinguish a pathogen-caused disease from a nutrient deficiency, and explain what a genetically modified crop is.

lessons.title: Paleobotany and Plant Evolution
lessons.objective: Order the major innovations in plant evolution and explain what each one made possible on land.
